newsitem.title: INDIA: India government finances under strain, says RBI. [CORRECTED 06:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: India government finances under strain, says RBI. [CORRECTED 06:40 GMT]

text.p: India's widening revenue and budget deficit in 1995/96 (April-March) reflected a continued strain on government finances, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Monday.
"The fiscal scenario was one of continued strain on the centre's finances as reflected in various deficit indicators," the RBI said in its "Report on Currency and Finance 1995/96."
It said the federal government's revenue deficit was higher at 333.31 billion rupees during 1995/96 compared to 310.29 billion rupees in 1994/95.
The budget deficit widened to 99.34 billion rupees during 1995/96 (corrects from 1996/97) from 9.46 billion ruperes in 1994/95.

"With the sharp rise in both the revenue and budget deficits, the monetised deficit, as measured by net RBI credit to the centre, shot up to 155.72 billion rupees, on a fortnightly average basis during 1995/96, in sharp contrast to a decline to 5.50 billion rupees in 1994/95," it said.
The revenue deficit refers to the difference between revenue expenditure and revenue income and excludes capital expenditure incurred by the government.
The substantial rise in all the deficit indicators was also reflected in the central government's gross fiscal deficit which rose to 640.10 billion rupees from 577.04 billion rupees in 1994/95.
"As proportion to GDP, the budget deficit as well as the monetised deficit widened even as the revenue deficit and the fiscal deficit came down during the year," the RBI said.
It said the budget deficit rose to 0.70 percent of GDP in 1995/96 from 0.10 percent in 1994/95.
The monetised deficit rose sharply to 1.83 percent of the GDP from 0.23 percent during the same period, it said.
